User-requested holistic audit pauses serial fixes and terminal approval. The main problem is composition of operation/admission and resource-completion ownership, not a list of unrelated timer bugs. Exact-primary compatibility plus a WeakMap cleanup side channel makes every retry/degrade consumer responsible for a guard; loader installs its guard in onRetry after the generic retry owner already classifies the error, contradicting the named before-classification contract. Adversarial accessor primaries expose that omission; public redefinable budget/target accessors also expose the difference between scalar validation and side-effect-free admission. These are contract counterexamples, not established causes of previous live formation failures. The stronger cross-layer D reproduction uses ordinary async cleanup and shows the parent can report stop while a probe cleanup still runs. Existing consumer receipt is restored to false; 606 focused assertions are behavior evidence only, not whole-boundary acceptance. No source implementation or live run during the holistic review; next change should consolidate the run-scope/attempt-outcome contract and compositional proof, not add one more local guard.
